title: NorthPoint POC weekly units & caching roundup
summary: Weekly POC sync covering tokens-per-dollar telemetry, caching effects on repeat queries, batching tradeoffs and an agreed 48h benchmark to validate economics. Customer leaning toward hosted pilot but wants latency tail analysis and security docs.
action_items: Priya Sharma: run 48h KV-only and KV+prefix caching benchmark, export token/cost CSV and histogram of tail latency - due 2026-11-27
Jordan Ellis: send updated pilot pricing sheet with dedicated vs hosted delta and burst policy notes - due 2026-11-24
Carlos Medina: provide 1 week of anonymized request traces (sample) for representative prompt distribution - due 2026-11-26
next_steps: Jordan to share pricing and security docs (SOC2 summary, KMS note)
Customer to share traces for better batching config
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-23 10:00 PT
Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Jordan Ellis (Redwood AE), Priya Sharma (Redwood SE), Carlos Medina (NorthPoint Head of ML), Aisha Grant (NorthPoint SRE), Tom Liao (Product)
---
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for jumping on, uh quick agenda - we'll walk telemetry from last week, caching numbers, batching tradeoffs and then decide on the 48 hour run. Sound good?
[00:15] Carlos: yep that's great, we got a couple people pulled into a different stand but should be fine.
[01:05] Priya: quick note, i pulled the summary metrics from the pilot cluster - this is on the hosted pilot with the rtx-like pool we've been using. numbers are raw before any prefix caching: median latency 90ms, p95 320ms, tokens/sec observed roughly 1,200 tokens/sec steady state on the 8k model variant. cost math: roughly 2,400 tokens per dollar in that config when you include model and infra amortized per hour.
[02:10] Aisha: 2,400 tokens per dollar, okay, and that's without caching?
[02:18] Priya: correct, that's without prefix or KV cache. once we enable KV cache for repeated contexts we saw effective tokens-per-dollar jump - in our small run it went to about 6,500 tokens per dollar for the top 60% of traffic which is pretty big. caveat: that's for high prompt reuse flows, if prompts are mostly unique the uplift is smaller, like 20-30%.
[03:05] Tom: can you explain the difference between prefix caching and KV cache in your numbers? i'm fuzzy on the difference.
[03:15] Priya: yeah totally. prefix caching caches the output of the first N tokens for identical prompt prefixes - so if you have boilerplate instructions that never change, prefix cache avoids re-encoding that. KV cache is token-level KV storage used during autoregressive generation; if users send repeated contexts or continuation patterns, the runtime reuses KV instead of recomputing attention. in practice KV gives higher savings for chatty multi-turn flows.
[04:00] Carlos: got it, so for our use-case (shipment status convo) we have very repetitive instructions but variable entity slots. sounds like prefix caching might handle that well.
[04:12] Priya: exactly. our quick experiment with prefix-only got about a 30-40% token savings versus baseline; KV plus prefix together hit that ~6.5k tokens/$ for the hotspot traffic.
[05:05] Jordan: important to flag the tradeoff - caching reduces tokens and cost but can add a tiny cache miss penalty and complexity around freshness/invalidations, e.g., if you need immediate real-time data in the prompt you have to avoid stale prefixes.
[06:00] Aisha: latency tail, has enabling batching hurt p95 for you? we care about occasional spikes because ops alerts are sensitive.
[06:12] Priya: yeah good question. batching raises throughput but can increase tail latency. in our last run, small batching windows (10-20ms) increased throughput by ~1.6x with negligible p95 impact. larger batches (50-100ms) pushed p95 from 320ms to ~520ms on the hosted pool. so we recommended adaptive batching: more aggressive batching when queue depth is high and a latency SLO gating layer to force immediate dispatch for high-priority routes.
[07:05] Carlos: can Redwood route by route? like make some endpoints low-latency and others high-throughput?
[07:15] Jordan: yep that's the routing policy we discussed earlier - per-route latency SLOs, and you can pin models or model variants. also fallback policies if preferred capacity exhausted.
[07:34] Carlos: thanks. Tom: i'm curious, how did quantization play into cost? any quality issues?
[07:45] Priya: we tried bfloat/INT8 quantized variants for the 8k model. quantization shaved about 12-18% off inference cost in the experiment and generally maintained quality on extraction/slot-filling tasks. for free-form generation there were edge-case regressions; we can run an eval harness on your prompts.
[08:30] Aisha: i want to see the tail distribution - do you have histograms?
[08:36] Priya: yes i attached a histogram to the notes but i'll export a higher-res CSV. quick numbers: median 90ms, p90 200ms, p95 320ms, p99 840ms baseline. with small batching p99 drops to ~620ms, with large batching p99 climbed to 1.2s.
[09:20] Carlos: hmm p99 840ms is fine mostly but 1.2s spikes trigger alerts.
[09:28] Jordan: that's why we want to tune adaptive batching + micro-batching policy plus route-level overrides. also worth mentioning Dedicated pool would reduce variance vs multi-tenant hosted pool - fewer noisy neighbors.
[10:10] Tom: what was the tokens/sec/$ delta you saw when moving from hosted to dedicated?
[10:20] Priya: dedicated lowers cost per token because of reserved capacity pricing. in our estimate: hosted baseline ~2,400 tokens/$; reserved dedicated model optimized with quant and batching can get to ~9,000 tokens/$ for repetitive workflows after caching. that's across idealized loads; realistic gains depend on utilization commit.
[11:05] Carlos: sounds promising but need to see hard numbers. we'll need 48h of representative traffic so utilization arithmetic is meaningful.
[11:15] Priya: agreed - that's the 48h run proposal: run two parallel configs for 48h against a sampled traffic replay: 1) hosted default with small adaptive batching + prefix caching; 2) dedicated-like config (same model variant quantized, more aggressive batching, KV+prefix). collect tokens, cost, latencies, and quality samples.
[12:02] Aisha: operationally we need to understand data residency and encryption - is KMS supported in hosted?
[12:12] Jordan: yes we support customer-managed KMS for Private/ Dedicated and for hosted we offer KMS integrations for enterprise plans. i'll attach SOC2 summary and KMS notes after the call.
[13:00] Carlos: any compliance caveats for PCI or HIPAA?
[13:08] Jordan: we have private/on-prem options for regulated workloads; for the hosted pilot we recommend redaction and tokenization of PHI until you're comfortable with the private deployment. also we can discuss our compliance add-ons.
[13:40] Tom: one more question on costs - do you show effective tokens per end-user session? our product team cares about cost per session not raw token numbers.
[13:52] Priya: yes we can map tokens-per-session using your sample traces. initial back-of-envelope: average session 350 tokens, at 2,400 tokens/$ that's about $0.145 per 1000 sessions? hold on, math: 350 tokens/session => 2.85 sessions per dollar? hmm i'm mixing. let me reframe: tokens/$ = 2,400 tokens per $1 => one session costs 0.145 cents? (there's a short math slip) we'll send an accurate sheet.
[15:00] Jordan: no problem, that's why we need the traces; Priya will run the session-level aggregation.
[16:35] Carlos: ok for the 48h run we can provide a sampled replay, sanitized, by end of Thursday.
[16:44] Jordan: perfect. we'll schedule the run for Friday and Monday results check-in next week.
[17:30] Aisha: one ops ask - what alerts should we set during the pilot? to avoid noisy pages.
[17:38] Priya: suggest alerting on sustained p95>500ms, error rate >1% over 5m, and queue backlog >500 requests which indicates batching increasing latency too much. also a cost burn monitor by tokens/hour.
[18:20] Tom: can Redwood send a config that we can import to our test infra? like a yaml?
[18:30] Jordan: yes we'll share route config templates and batching configs.
[19:05] Carlos: wonderful. any blockers on your side?
[19:12] Priya: none, just need your traces and confirmation of windows to run.
[20:00] Jordan: recap - Priya: run 48h benchmarks, Jordan: pricing & security docs, Carlos: traces. follow-up 2026-11-30. Anything else?
[20:18] Tom: just, please call out assumptions in the pricing sheet - e.g., reserved utilization %.
[20:25] Jordan: will do. thanks everyone.
